newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DETROIT SINKS SHARKS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DETROIT SINKS SHARKS.

text.p: Steve Yzerman celebrated his new contract with a goal and three assists and Mike Vernon stopped 24 shots as the Detroit Red Wings routed the San Jose Sharks 5-1 Friday.

Yzerman, who signed a four-year contract extension earlier this week, continued his brillance against the Sharks. In 18 career meetings with San Jose, the Red Wings captain has seven goals and 23 points. The Sharks have never won a regular-season game in Detroit and are just 2-17-1 all-time against the Red Wings.
Greg Hawgood had the lone goal for San Jose, his first since March 24th, 1995.

At Florida, Ray Sheppard and Stu Barnes scored 10 seconds apart late in the second period, lifting the Florida Panthers into a 3-3 tie with the New York Islanders in a battle between the Atlantic Division's best and worst teams.
Mike Hough had the other goal for the Panthers, who own the league's best record at 11-2-5.
"I thought we battled back," said Panthers coach Doug MacLean. "It was good to come back from two down, but we didn't have our legs and we didn't have any jump tonight."
In Ottawa, rookie Andreas Dackell scored with 2:45 left in the third period to help the Ottawa Senators snap a three-game losing streak with a 4-3 victory over the Chicago Blackhawks.

With the game tied, 3-3, Denny Lambert picked up a loose puck in the neutral zone and skated down the left side. He fed a pass into the slot to a cutting Dackell, who moved in a stride and put a shot through goaltender Jeff Hackett's pads for his fourth goal of the season.
Wade Redden, Steve Duchesne and Randy Cunneyworth also scored for Ottawa.
In Washington, Jim Carey made 30 saves and Kelly Miller's first goal of the season was the game-winner as the Washington Capitals beat the Montreal Canadiens 3-1.
Peter Bondra and Sergei Gonchar also scored for the Caps (9-9), who have won three of their last four games to climb to the .500 mark for the first time this season.
Brian Savage had the lone goal for Montreal, which fell to 2-7-1 in its last 10 games.
In Dallas, Sergei Zubov and Jamie Langenbrunner scored 3:57 apart in the third period as the Dallas Stars continued their dominance of the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim with a come-from-behind 4-3 victory.
Joe Sacco and Teemu Selanne scored 33 seconds apart late in the second period to give the Ducks a 3-2 lead, but the Stars drew even 4:21 into the third on Zubov's power-play goal.
Andy Moog made 18 saves for Dallas, which has won 11 of its last 12 meetings with the Ducks.
